title: SWE-rebench: Lessons from Evaluating Coding Agents — Ibragim Badertdinov, Nebius
talk_summary: The talk presents SWE-rebench, a monthly benchmark of fresh real-world GitHub issues run in Docker with fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests across many models and a common harness. It distills practical lessons on eval construction, caching, retry/error classification, reward hacking, model-version drift, and code-quality gaps in agent patches.

takeaways.technique: Fresh internal validation set with repeated trials
takeaways.what_they_do: They collect recent real issues/PRs, build Docker snapshots, verify fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests, and run each task multiple times to report pass@5 and pass-all-5 reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do five runs per each uh task to report some confidence intervals and also pass at five
takeaways.numbers: 5 runs per task; 30 models evaluated monthly; sample kept 10% larger than final need

takeaways.what_they_do: They use provider caching and a minimal ReAct-style harness, avoiding over-engineered agents and unnecessary context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with the caching included, you your cost will be like four times less
takeaways.numbers: ~4x lower cost with caching for their simple agent

takeaways.technique: Classify model vs infrastructure errors before retrying
takeaways.what_they_do: They define retry policy by exit status, separating model failures such as too-long context or too-many tool calls from provider/infrastructure errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to define what exit status, for example, uh too long context or too many tool calls or your provider errors

takeaways.technique: Block future-history and network reward hacking
takeaways.what_they_do: They remove future Git history from sandbox checkouts and restrict web/curl access after agents used them to find the original solution patch or issue discussion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we remove all the future Git history

takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that reasoning/caching defaults drift across model versions and recommend running an external benchmark on your own infrastructure before trusting reported numbers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there could be some default parameters drifting for the reasoning level, for the caching level

takeaways.technique: Check for leftover repro files and patch hygiene
takeaways.what_they_do: They observe agent patches often include reproduction tests or files that are never removed, which real reviewers would reject.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they tend to produce some reproduce tests or files and then just don't remove it
